Compute the numbers of a descriptive table

Source: R/table1.R
table1.Rd

table1() computes the numbers of a descriptive table, per group and for all rows. With a style, it also formats these numbers as text.

Usage

table1(d, by, vars, style = NULL)

Arguments

d

A data.table, or a data.frame.

by

The name of the grouping column in d.

vars

A data.table with the columns var and type. var names a column in d. type is "bin" for a 0/1 variable, "cont" for a numeric variable, or "cat" for a categorical variable. Two text columns are optional. label is the printed label of the variable, and NA gives its name. section names the section that the variable belongs to, and NA or "" gives none.

style

NULL, the name of an installed style, or the path to a style file that ends in .yml. table1_styles() gives the names of the installed styles. With NULL, table1() does no formatting. The section Styles below describes a style file.

Value

A data.table with one row per variable and group, in the order of vars, and "All" first. A "cat" variable has one row per level and group. The columns are var, grp, n, missing, mean, sd, events, pct, p, test, level, median, q1 and q3. n counts the non-missing values. pbn 2026.12.3 added the last four columns. The column label follows, which pbn 2026.12.4 added: the label of the variable, or the level of a level row. With a style, the columns row, value_pretty (the cell text) and p_pretty (the text of p) follow. The attribute footnotes then holds the footnotes of the style as a character vector. A style can add rows, as the section Styles says. The other columns of each row of the output without a style stay the same.

Details

The groups are the levels of by, plus "All". The levels are the factor levels when by is a factor, and the sorted unique values otherwise. A row with a missing by counts in "All" only. A level of by that is "All" is an error. A level with no rows has a row in the output with n = 0.

For a "bin" variable:

  • events is the count of 1, and pct is 100 * events / n.

  • p compares the levels of by that have a non-missing value. It comes from the Pearson chi-square test without continuity correction. When any expected count is below 5, it comes from Fisher's exact test.

  • Fisher's exact test first uses the default workspace of stats::fisher.test(). When the test stops with that workspace, it runs again with a workspace of 2e7. When it also stops then, p is NA, test is "fisher_failed", and a warning names the variable. A p of Fisher's exact test is exact, never simulated.

  • test is "chisq", "fisher" or "fisher_failed", and it is the same on every row of the variable. When fewer than two levels have a non-missing value, p and test are NA.

  • A value other than 0, 1 or NA is an error.

For a "cont" variable, mean, sd, median, q1 and q3 hold the numbers of the non-missing values. q1 and q3 are the first and the third quartile. The median and the quartiles are stats::quantile() with type = 7, the default of R. p and test are NA in this version.

A "cat" variable has one row for each level and group. The rows of a level are together, in the order of the groups.

  • The levels are the factor levels when the variable is a factor. Otherwise they are the sorted unique values that are not NA, so a number sorts as a number. level holds each level as text.

  • events is the count of the level, and n is the count of the non-missing values of the group. So pct is 100 * events / n, and the percentages of a group with n above 0 add up to 100.

  • p and test follow the rule of a "bin" variable, with the levels in place of 0 and 1. A level with a count of 0 in each group is not part of the test. When fewer than two levels or fewer than two groups remain, p and test are NA.

  • A variable that has no level, because each value is NA and it is not a factor, has one row per group. Its level, events and pct are NA. With a style it gets no level row, only its heading row and the Missing row that missing.show asks for.

A column that does not apply to the type holds NA.

Styles

A style formats the numbers of table1() for a journal or a report. A style can only format what table1() computes. It cannot add a test of a "cont" variable.

An installed style is the file inst/table1/<name>_<YYYY_MM_DD>.yml of pbn. Its name is the file name without .yml. pbn never edits a released style, so a changed style gets a new date.

A style file is a YAML map of sections. Each field of a section is a map with the keys value and source. source is one string that says where the value comes from. table1() takes any source that is not empty. The source of an installed style MUST cite a reference table or a guideline page, as the subsection on the proof of a style says. table1() checks every field when it reads the file. An unknown field, a missing field, a missing source or a value that the field does not allow stops it. The error names the field and the file. The fields that pbn 2026.12.3 added are optional, so a style file of an earlier pbn stays valid. They are cont.median_digits, the section cat, and the fields missing.row_template and missing.row_pct_digits. pbn 2026.12.4 added the optional fields cat.level_prefix and missing.row_label. An optional field that is present gets the same checks as the other fields.

A template is text with placeholders in braces, such as {events}. A template can hold only the placeholders of its field, in any order, and it can hold none. These are the fields:

  • bin.template: the cell of a "bin" row, over {events}, {n} and {pct}. An example is "{events} ({pct})".

  • bin.pct_digits: the decimals of pct, a whole number from 0 to 10.

  • cont.template: the cell of a "cont" row, over {mean}, {sd}, {median}, {q1} and {q3}. An example is "{median} ({q1}-{q3})". A template that holds {median}, {q1} or {q3} needs cont.median_digits.

  • cont.mean_digits and cont.sd_digits: the decimals of mean and of sd, each a whole number from 0 to 10.

  • cont.median_digits (optional): the decimals of median, q1 and q3, a whole number from 0 to 10.

  • cat (an optional section): it MUST be present when vars has a "cat" variable. When it is present, it MUST hold the three fields below that are not optional.

  • cat.template: the cell of a level row of a "cat" variable, over {events}, {n} and {pct}, as bin.template.

  • cat.pct_digits: the decimals of pct in a level row, a whole number from 0 to 10.

  • cat.heading_template: the cell of the heading row of a "cat" variable. It holds no placeholder. "" gives an empty cell.

  • cat.level_prefix (optional): the text before the level in the column label of a level row, such as "- ".

  • p.digits: the decimals of p, a whole number from 0 to 10.

  • p.template: the text of p, over {p}. "P ={p}" gives P =0.005, and "{p}" gives the number only.

  • p.lower: null, or a number above 0 and below 1. A p below it gets p.below_template in place of p.template.

  • p.below_template: the text of such a p, over {lower}. With p.lower 0.001, "P <{lower}" gives P <0.001.

  • p.upper: null, or a number above 0 and below 1. A p above it gets p.above_template.

  • p.above_template: the text of such a p, over {upper}. With p.upper 0.999, "P >{upper}" gives P >0.999.

  • thousands.mark: the thousands separator, such as ",". The empty string "" gives no separator.

  • thousands.from: a number above 0. A number gets the separator when its rounded absolute value is thousands.from or more. With 10000, 12347 prints as 12,347 and 9999 prints as 9999.

  • missing.show: never, if_any, always, row_if_any or row_always. With if_any, a cell gets missing.template when missing is above 0. With always, each cell that is not NA gets it. With row_if_any, a variable gets a Missing row when its "All" group has a missing value. With row_always, each variable gets a Missing row. The two row choices need missing.row_template.

  • missing.template: the text that table1() adds to the end of a cell, over {missing}. An example is "; {missing} missing". Only if_any and always use it.

  • missing.row_template (optional): the cell of a Missing row, over {missing} and {pct}. An example is "{missing} ({pct}%)". The template "{missing}" gives the missing count only, such as "2".

  • missing.row_pct_digits (optional): the decimals of pct in a Missing row, a whole number from 0 to 10. A Missing row needs it only when missing.row_template holds {pct}.

  • missing.row_label (optional): the column label of a Missing row, such as "Missing". Without it, the label is NA.

  • footnotes: a list, which can be empty. Each item is a map with the keys value and source, and value is the text of one footnote.

p.lower and p.upper print with p.digits decimals, so each MUST have no more decimals than p.digits. p.lower MUST be below p.upper. table1() compares p with the thresholds before it rounds p, so 0.9994 is above 0.999. A p equal to a threshold gets p.template.

A style can add rows, and the column row names the kind of each row:

  • "value": a row of the output without a style. A level row of a "cat" variable has p_pretty NA.

  • "heading": one row for each group before the level rows of a "cat" variable. Its cell is cat.heading_template, and its p_pretty is the P of the variable.

  • "missing": one row for each group after the other rows of a variable, when missing.show asks for it. Its cell gives missing and its percent, and its column pct holds that percent, 100 * missing / (n + missing). The denominator counts every row of the group, missing ones included. Its p_pretty is NA.

  • "section": one row for each group before the rows of the first variable of each section, when vars has the column section. Its grp is the group and its label is the section. Each other column is NA.

The column label of a heading row is the label of the variable. A level row has cat.level_prefix and the level, and a Missing row has missing.row_label.

A heading row and a Missing row keep var, grp, n, missing, p and test of the group. Their level and their other numbers are NA, except pct of a Missing row. A table with no "cat" variable, no Missing row and no section keeps the rows of the output without a style.

table1() rounds each number with formatC(), which rounds as the C function sprintf() does. events, n and missing print with no decimals. The thousands separator applies to every number of a cell. A cell is NA when a number of its template is NA, as for a group with n = 0. p_pretty is NA where p is NA.

The proof of a style

pbn installs a style only with the real published Table 1s that prove it. Beside the file inst/table1/<name>.yml is the folder inst/table1/<name>/. For each reference table k, it holds five files:

  • reference_<k>.csv: the table as printed. It has one row per printed row and one column per printed column. The header holds the printed column headers, and the first column holds the printed row labels. Each cell is the printed string, and an empty cell is "".

  • source_<k>.yml: the fields authors, title, journal, year, volume, pages, doi, table and transcribed. authors is a list of maps with the keys family and given. pages is the article number or the pages, and table is the number of the table. transcribed is a map with the keys file, by and date.

  • fake_<k>.csv: the fake data, one row per fake person. An empty cell or NA is a missing value.

  • vars_<k>.csv: the columns var, type, label, levels and section. The one row of type by names the column of the groups. The other rows, with var, type, label and section, are the argument vars. levels gives the order of the groups, or of the levels of a "cat" variable, separated by |. levels and section can be empty.

  • layout_<k>.yml: the map of the output onto the printed table. Each item of columns names a printed column, except the first, in order. It has cell: value and a grp, or cell: p. Each item of rows names a printed row, in order. It has the key row and, where it applies, var and level, and no other key. row is value, heading or missing as in the column row of the output. It is section for a section heading, and none for a printed row with no computed counterpart.

The test of pbn runs table1(fake, by, vars, style) for each reference table. It compares each printed cell with the cell of the style, the row labels of the first column included. The headers are not cells. The cell of the style is value_pretty of the group, or p_pretty for cell: p, and NA is "". The label of the style is the column label of the same row of the output. No label comes from the layout or the reference. A printed row of section takes the label of the section row of the output. That row MUST come right before the first row of the next variable of the layout, and the label is "" without it. A row of section has "" in each cell after the label. A row of none has "" in each cell. So each printed cell of it that is not empty MUST be an exception with the rule not_computable.

A cell passes when the two strings are identical. A cell that differs passes only when the file exceptions.yml of the folder lists it with the same two strings.

exceptions.yml is a map with the one key exceptions, a list. Each item has these fields:

  • reference, row and column: the cell, as reference_1, the number of the printed row after the header, and the printed header.

  • printed and style: the printed string and the string of the style.

  • rule, source and justification: why the two differ. source and justification MUST NOT be empty.

rule is one of these:

  • guideline: the reference departs from the author guidelines, and the style follows them. source names the guideline and its page.

  • other_reference: two references disagree, and the style follows the other one. source cites a cell of the other reference.

  • not_computable: table1() cannot compute the cell, such as a P of a "cont" variable.

  • published_error: the printed cell is wrong. source gives the computation that shows it.

The test fails a style in each of these cases:

  • A cell differs, and exceptions.yml does not list it.

  • An exception has strings other than those of its cell. A cell that matches MUST NOT have an exception.

  • An exception names no cell, or a cell twice.

  • The style has no folder. The folder lacks a file, or it holds a file of another name.

  • The source of a field holds "editorial", in any case.

  • The source of a field cites none of the three forms of a citation:

    1. a cell, as reference_1, row 2, column "P".

    2. the family name of the first author of a reference, with Table <n> of its source.

    3. a guide or a guideline with its page, as p. 4 or page 4.

A style that pbn cannot prove is withdrawn. pbn removes its file and keeps its name, so table1() stops with the version that withdrew it and the reason. table1_styles() does not list it. pbn 2026.12.4 withdrew ijoa_brief_report_2026_11_20, because it was not proven against real published tables.

See also

Other shared helpers: table1_styles()

Examples

d <- data.table::data.table(
  g = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
  smoker = rep(c(1, 0, 0, 1), 5),
  age = 21:40
)
vars <- data.table::data.table(
  var = c("smoker", "age"),
  type = c("bin", "cont")
)
pbn::table1(d, by = "g", vars = vars)
#>       var    grp     n missing  mean      sd events   pct     p   test  level
#>    <char> <char> <int>   <int> <num>   <num>  <int> <num> <num> <char> <char>
#> 1: smoker    All    20       0    NA      NA     10    50     1  chisq   <NA>
#> 2: smoker      a    10       0    NA      NA      5    50     1  chisq   <NA>
#> 3: smoker      b    10       0    NA      NA      5    50     1  chisq   <NA>
#> 4:    age    All    20       0  30.5 5.91608     NA    NA    NA   <NA>   <NA>
#> 5:    age      a    10       0  25.5 3.02765     NA    NA    NA   <NA>   <NA>
#> 6:    age      b    10       0  35.5 3.02765     NA    NA    NA   <NA>   <NA>
#>    median    q1    q3  label
#>     <num> <num> <num> <char>
#> 1:     NA    NA    NA smoker
#> 2:     NA    NA    NA smoker
#> 3:     NA    NA    NA smoker
#> 4:   30.5 25.75 35.25    age
#> 5:   25.5 23.25 27.75    age
#> 6:   35.5 33.25 37.75    age

# A style file, written to tempdir()
style <- file.path(tempdir(), "example_2026_12_01.yml")
writeLines(c(
  "bin:",
  "  template: {value: '{events} ({pct})', source: example only}",
  "  pct_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}",
  "cont:",
  "  template: {value: '{mean} ({sd})', source: example only}",
  "  mean_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}",
  "  sd_digits: {value: 1, source: example only}",
  "p:",
  "  digits: {value: 3, source: example only}",
  "  template: {value: 'P ={p}', source: example only}",
  "  lower: {value: 0.001, source: example only}",
  "  below_template: {value: 'P <{lower}', source: example only}",
  "  upper: {value: 0.999, source: example only}",
  "  above_template: {value: 'P >{upper}', source: example only}",
  "thousands:",
  "  mark: {value: ',', source: example only}",
  "  from: {value: 10000, source: example only}",
  "missing:",
  "  show: {value: if_any, source: example only}",
  "  template: {value: '; {missing} missing', source: example only}",
  "footnotes:",
  "  - {value: 'Values are n (percent) or mean (SD).', source: example only}"
), style)
t1 <- pbn::table1(d, by = "g", vars = vars, style = style)
t1[, c("var", "grp", "value_pretty", "p_pretty")]
#>       var    grp value_pretty p_pretty
#>    <char> <char>       <char>   <char>
#> 1: smoker    All    10 (50.0) P >0.999
#> 2: smoker      a     5 (50.0) P >0.999
#> 3: smoker      b     5 (50.0) P >0.999
#> 4:    age    All   30.5 (5.9)     <NA>
#> 5:    age      a   25.5 (3.0)     <NA>
#> 6:    age      b   35.5 (3.0)     <NA>
attr(t1, "footnotes")
#> [1] "Values are n (percent) or mean (SD)."
